subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up — concurrency & rate limits (Acme)
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>

Cc: Sabrina Lee <sabrina.lee@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO follow-up — concurrency & rate limits

Thanks for the time today, Marissa — good convo. Quick recap from our side and some additional detail you asked for: 

- High-level targets:
  - Latency: target end-to-end P95 for typical responses (average ~150 tokens) <= 700ms.
  - Streaming: time-to-first-byte (TTFB) for streamed responses <= 200ms for 95% of requests.
  - Throughput: sustained token throughput ~25k tokens/sec during peak windows.

- Concurrency profile:
  - Steady-state concurrent requests: ~250 parallel calls.
  - Spiky bursts: up to ~1000 parallel calls for short windows (5-10 minutes) during product launches.
  - Connection behavior: our app keeps persistent HTTP/2 connections and does connection pooling; we re-use connections across requests where possible.

- Failure tolerance / fallbacks:
  - We need graceful degradation if quota is hit — prefer 429 + Retry-After vs. hard failures.

Attached is our internal SLO worksheet with request mix by endpoint. Can you confirm whether Redwood’s hosted rate limits or Dedicated plans can handle the burst profile? Also curious what the typical concurrency quotas are and how we can request a temporary bump for launches.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick follow-up if that’s easier.

--
Alex Johnson
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Cloud
Attachment: acme-slo-requirements.xlsx (XLSX)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up — concurrency & rate limits

Alex — thanks for the clear recap and the worksheet. Looping in Laura (solutions engineering) and Logan (platform) to weigh in on quota mechanics and connection tuning.

Quick answers and next steps:

1) Hosted rate limits today
   - Default: 60 requests/minute per API key and a soft concurrency limit of ~20 concurrent reqs per key.
   - We can increase per-customer request rates and concurrency via account-level rate limits for paid accounts, but very large sustained concurrency typically needs Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity).

2) How we meet your SLOs
   - Latency (P95 <= 700ms): reasonable for short responses on our optimized GPUs with continuous batching, provided the average prompt length and model selection align (we recommend a latency-optimized model variant).
   - Streaming TTFB <= 200ms: supported; we optimize for fast first-token emission. Best practice is to use persistent HTTP/2 connections and enable our streaming endpoints.
   - Throughput / burst handling: sustained 25k tokens/sec can be handled with Dedicated or a large hosted allocation -- we can size reserved concurrency accordingly.

3) Concurrency & connection pooling
   - We recommend re-using HTTP/2 connections, keeping keep-alive enabled, and using a small pool (10-30 sockets) per host in your client to limit connection churn.
   - For your burst profile (250 steady -> 1,000 peak), we propose:
      a) Increase account-level concurrency to 400 for hosted to start (soft limit), with an agreed ramp plan.
      b) For launches, a temporary burst window managed by a dedicated reservation or on-call capacity bump to ~1000 concurrent slots for 10-15 minutes.

4) Rate-limit behavior / retries
   - We return 429 with Retry-After; we also provide quota status headers so you can implement backpressure. For critical flows we recommend pre-warming or using reserved concurrency.

Next steps: I’ll attach a short proposal with two options (hosted bump + ramp plan vs. Dedicated reserved pool) and rough pricing. Laura -- can you take point on sizing and technical onboarding? Logan -- can you confirm feasibility of temporary burst windows from an infra perspective?

I’ve attached the proposal PDF.

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Performance SLO follow-up — concurrency & rate limits

Thanks for the worksheet, Alex — pulled a couple of numbers and sketched sizing. Key notes:

- Model choice: recommend latency-optimized 8-bit quantized variant (low token latency with good throughput).
- Reserved concurrency sizing:
  - Baseline reserved concurrency: 400 slots to cover steady-state with headroom.
  - Burst pool: additional 600 slots available as temporary reservation for launches (activated via a short request window; we can automate activation via our console or an API call).
- Token throughput: given your 25k tokens/sec peak, the above mix looks sufficient on a Dedicated pool of 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs with the right batching profile.

Operational recommendations:
- Use connection pooling + HTTP/2; set idle timeout to 60s and pool size 20 per app server.
- Implement exponential backoff with jitter and honor Retry-After header.

I’ll prepare a short runbook for the activation process (how to request a burst window, expected lead times, and SLA implications).

--
Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Cost ballpark (monthly):

  - Dedicated reserved pool (4xA100-equivalent): ~$55k-70k/mo (flat reserved fee) -- this includes predictable latency, capacity isolation, and faster burst activation SLAs.
